title: The Danish Maritime Authority probe has answered 'reachable' on none of its recorded attempts, a pattern the code's own comment dates to a single night
statement: darkocean/sources.py's module docstring (lines 15-17) reads: 'DMA (Denmark) day dumps would carry the per-moment declared axis; the source failed three probes on 2026-08-08 and is probed (never fetched) each night until it answers -- an outage is recorded, not bridged.' That sentence names one date. autonomy/log.jsonl carries four darkocean-run entries, one per night darkocean has actually executed (2026-08-07, 2026-08-08, 2026-08-11, 2026-08-12 -- the only four; 2026-08-09 through 2026-08-11 minus the 11th were lost to the anchor deadlock, obs-2026-08-11-1.json/obs-2026-08-12-1.json), and every one of the four carries `"dma": "outage: URLError"`. Zero of four recorded probes have ever returned `probe_dma`'s other possible state, `reachable (HTTP ...)` (practice/src/practice/darkocean/sources.py, probe_dma, lines 121-131). The source has not answered on any night the observatory has a record of, spanning nearly the full life of the practice (2026-08-07 to 2026-08-12) -- not only 2026-08-08.
method: python3 -c "import json; [print(json.loads(l)['ts'], json.loads(l)['detail'].get('date'), json.loads(l)['detail'].get('dma')) for l in open('autonomy/log.jsonl') if json.loads(l).get('step')=='darkocean-run']" -- read every darkocean-run entry's `dma` field directly. Read darkocean/sources.py's module docstring and probe_dma (lines 121-131) for the two states the field can hold and what the docstring itself claims.
worth_watching_because: This is not a claim that the Danish Maritime Authority's service is down right now, or a claim about why -- only a record-vs-record fact: the practice's own code comment frames the outage as a dated, singular event ('failed three probes on 2026-08-08'), while the practice's own log shows the identical outage on 100% of the four nights it has a record of since, unremarked in any later commit. darkocean/METHOD.md's source table already calls DMA 'probed nightly, not yet fetched' and treats an outage as an honest, unbridged fact rather than a failure -- so nothing here says the design is wrong. What the accumulated nights add that the 2026-08-08 comment alone could not: a reader trusting that one dated sentence would not know the probe has never once succeeded, or how many nights of trying that now represents. Left alone, the comment stays anchored to the first night indefinitely while the record it describes keeps growing past it.
left_alone: No repair proposed: probe_dma's own doc-comment staleness is a narrative-accuracy question, not a defect a test can catch or a behavior a falsification clause could bind, and the underlying design (probe, never fetch, record the outage honestly) is already exactly what darkocean/METHOD.md says it is. Not proposing a sensor either -- with a single probed-only source and every recorded night identical, a threshold or N-consecutive-nights rule would have nothing to distinguish yet; worth reconsidering if a second probed-only source is ever added, or if DMA answers even once and then stops again.
